case.question: I fish from the pier for salmon. For this week, how good do you expect pier fishing for salmon to be at each of St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon? Rate each port 0-4 (0 slow, 1 below average, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent) and say which you'd go to.

events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to St. Joseph.** It's my best pick, but expect only slow to below-average pier salmon fishing this week.
- Pier ratings for this week (my estimates, not DNR ratings):
  - St. Joseph: 1 (below average), the best option
  - South Haven: 1
  - Grand Haven: 1
  - Muskegon: 0 (slow), least data
- If the pier is slow, the boat fishing reported at St. Joseph was the best of the four ports. Plan on deep water, 100 ft or more.

## Why

- The DNR reports have no pier salmon reports for any of these four ports in the last six weeks. Every salmon report is from boat anglers, so these pier ratings are my inference.
- St. Joseph had the strongest recent boat reports: "decent" on July 5 and "good" on June 21 (St. Joseph, 2023-07-05; St. Joseph, 2023-06-21). I'd expect that to carry over to the pier somewhat.
- Surface water is warm, around 70 F, and the buoys show no upwelling drop. I'd expect the pier bite to stay weak until a cold-water upwelling arrives (Conditions now).
- Past July weeks with water near 70 F were mostly slow for boats (historical reports from 2022), which is why I'd expect slow pier fishing too (Past seasons).

## Evidence

**Recent reports**
- St. Joseph, 2023-07-05: boat, quality 2 (average), fishing "well beyond 120 feet," surface water 71 F.
- St. Joseph, 2023-06-21: boat, quality 3 (good), 80 to 120 ft, most fish on shrimp.
- South Haven, 2023-07-05: boat, quality 1, "very deep water," about 100 ft, spoons.
- Grand Haven, 2023-06-21: boat, quality 2, fish 35 to 90 ft down in 65 to 160 ft, orange spoons and green or yellow meat rigs.
- Muskegon, 2023-06-07: boat, quality 1, slow, fish 30 to 100 ft down in 70 to 180 ft. This is 41 days old.

**Past seasons (similar water, about 70 F, within 3 weeks of today)**
- Mostly slow to below-average boat fishing, with fish deep: Grand Haven 2022-07-14 (quality 0, 100 to 180 ft), Muskegon 2022-07-14 (quality 0, 100 to 200 ft), South Haven 2022-07-06 (quality 0, "well beyond 100 feet").
- St. Joseph 2022-07-06 was the one past week with some promise: "the best water seemed to be in 30 to 40 feet of water," but fish were mostly deeper than 100 ft.

**Conditions now**
- The conditions tool returned a backtest summary for the week before 2023-07-18, not live data. Buoy surface water was 71 F at St. Joseph (flat over the week), 71 F at South Haven (+2 F), and 68 F at Grand Haven and Muskegon (+4 F).
- No modeled pierhead water temperature or cold-layer depth came back, so I can't judge pier upwelling directly.

## Caveats

- No pier reports exist for these ports in the recent database, so the pier ratings are estimates from boat reports and past seasons.
- The newest reports are from July 5 (13 days old) for St. Joseph and South Haven. Grand Haven's is from June 21 (27 days old), and Muskegon's is from June 7 (41 days old).
- The current conditions are a backtest summary, not live readings. Check the live buoy and pierhead temperatures before you go. A sharp drop in surface temperature would suggest upwelling, which would improve pier chances.
- The 2022 comparisons are general history, not this week's conditions.

- DNR bulletin, June 21 (Grand Haven, South Haven, St. Joseph): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3614332
- DNR bulletin, June 7 (Grand Haven, Muskegon): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/35ed629
